brief_data.deck: Supabase, the open-source Postgres backend that more than 9 million developers build on, closed a $500M Series F led by GIC at a $10.5B post-money valuation on 4 June 2026, doubling the $5B it set eight months earlier and taking total funding past $1B.

risks.label: DEVELOPER-LED BRAND
risks.detail: Supabase grew on open source and community with no chief marketing officer; a Formula 1 spend is off-pattern.
risks.counter: Frame it as developer reach, not a billboard: Claude, Atlassian and the paddock as a developer stage, paid partly in credits.

risks.label: VALUATION PACE
risks.detail: A valuation doubled in eight months invites scrutiny; a visible sponsorship can read as excess to investors.
risks.counter: Size the entry modestly, tie it to measurable developer sign-ups, and announce it alongside product news such as Multigres.

extended.ask: A 25-minute call with Paul Copplestone before the British GP to walk through the Claude Code connection, agree a Silverstone or Austin announcement window, and size an Official Developer Platform Partner entry against Williams' 2027 roster.

value.text: Supabase provides the Postgres database, authentication, storage and realtime layer for the applications Williams ships around the car: fan and ticketing apps, partner and hospitality portals, and the internal dashboards and tools engineers and strategists build with Claude. Multigres, released in preview with the round, gives those systems horizontal scale on race weekends when traffic spikes.
value.label: Operational workstream (Mode A)

value.text: A platform used by more than 9 million developers brings a developer audience Williams' existing partners want to reach, plus a guest list of founders, investors and enterprise engineering leaders for the British GP and the US rounds.
value.label: Commercial lift for the team

value.text: Co-produced engineering content with the Claude programme: how a race team builds and ships software in a week, the coding agent and the database on one car, and a factory reference customer for Supabase's enterprise sales.
value.label: Content and ecosystem

value.text: Official Developer Platform Partner designation, sidepod or engine-cover placement, British GP and US-round hospitality, driver and engineering access for Supabase's channels, and a developer-community activation at Silverstone.
value.label: What the team gives back

why_now.text: On 4 June 2026 Supabase announced a $500M Series F led by GIC at a $10.5B post-money valuation, with Accel, Y Combinator, Craft, Felicis, Peak XV and Coatue returning, Stripe investing for a second time and Salesforce Ventures joining. Total capital raised now exceeds $1B. The company announced it on its own blog; CNBC and TechCrunch confirmed the figures.
why_now.label: Trigger

why_now.text: The Series E in October 2025 priced the company at $5B; the Series D in April 2025 at $2B. A company re-priced from $2B to $10.5B inside fourteen months has a story to tell enterprise buyers and, eventually, public markets, and now has the budget to tell it.
why_now.label: Valuation doubled in eight months

why_now.text: Supabase says database launches on its platform grew 600% in the past year and that over 60% of new databases are created by AI tools, with Claude Code the largest contributor since the start of 2026. That is the same Claude that races on the Williams: the partnership story writes itself.
why_now.label: The AI-coding tailwind

why_now.text: The British GP on 5 July is Williams' home race and sits five weeks from the announcement; the United States GP in Austin and the Las Vegas GP follow in the autumn, close to Supabase's US customer base. Teams settle their 2027 partner rosters in the fourth quarter, so a deal agreed over the summer can launch in full for 2027.
why_now.label: Calendar window

why_team.text: Williams carries Atlassian as title partner, VAST for data infrastructure, Keeper for identity security, Airia and Brillio on the technology side and Claude as Official Thinking Partner. No database, backend or developer-platform brand is on the car: Official Developer Platform Partner is a clean category at a team-partner price.
why_team.label: The open lane

why_team.text: Supabase's own funding announcement names Claude Code as the biggest creator of new Supabase databases this year. Claude has been on the Williams since the February livery reveal, working with the team's engineers and strategists. The introduction can run through a relationship Williams already has, and the activation can pair the coding agent with the database it builds on.
why_team.label: The warm path

why_team.text: Atlassian sells to the same software teams Supabase does. A Williams sponsorship puts Supabase next to Jira, Bitbucket and Claude on the one car in Formula 1 that already reads as a developer stack, rather than as a lone logo on a consumer-brand livery.
why_team.label: A roster that speaks to developers

why_team.text: A remote-first company with founders from outside Silicon Valley and a global developer community fits a British team with a global fan base and US ambitions. The British GP gives a home stage; Austin and Las Vegas give the US one.
why_team.label: Story and market fit

ruled_out.reason: Oracle is title partner and the database incumbent; a direct category conflict.
Google Cloud (owner of Firebase, the product Supabase positions itself against) and Dell hold the cloud and hardware lanes.
Microsoft holds the cloud lane at both; SAP also sits on the Mercedes.
IBM, HP and DXC Technology cover data, compute and cloud services.
Confluent (data streaming) and Dynatrace occupy the adjacent data lanes; crowded.
NetApp, CoreWeave, Cognizant and ServiceNow make the technology roster crowded; no developer-ecosystem tie.
Core Scientific, TWG AI and IFS hold the compute, AI and software lanes on the inaugural roster.

ruled_out.team: Audi F1 Team · TGR Haas F1 Team
ruled_out.reason: Open but not chosen: neither carries the Claude tie that gives Williams a warm path.

brief_data.bottom_line: A $500M raise at $10.5B, more than 9 million developers, and Claude Code as the top creator of Supabase databases put Supabase at peak brand-investment capacity with a warm route onto the one car Claude already races on. The developer-platform lane at Williams is open and the British GP sits inside the window.

brief_data.the_case_p1: Supabase announced on 4 June a $500M Series F led by GIC, with Accel, Y Combinator, Craft, Felicis, Peak XV and Coatue returning, a second investment from Stripe and a first from Salesforce Ventures. The post-money valuation is $10.5B, up from $5B at the October 2025 Series E and $2B at the April 2025 Series D; total capital raised now exceeds $1B. The company reports more than 250,000 customers and over 9 million developers, and says database launches grew 600% in the past year, with over 60% created by AI coding tools.
brief_data.the_case_p2: The grid has already priced developer infrastructure: Atlassian holds the Williams title, Oracle sits on the Red Bull, Google Cloud and Dell on the McLaren. What none of them owns is the open-source Postgres layer beneath the AI-coding boom. Supabase says Claude Code has been the largest single creator of new databases on its platform this year, and Claude already races on the Williams. That is a warm path, not a cold call.

brief_data.value_content: MODE A - operational. Supabase is the Postgres, authentication and realtime backend for the software Williams ships around the car: fan and ticketing apps, partner portals, and the internal tools engineers build with Claude. Multigres, previewed with the round, gives those systems scale on race weekends. In return: Official Developer Platform designation, sidepod placement, British GP hospitality and a co-produced engineering series with the Claude programme.
brief_data.why_team_para: Williams carries the most developer-native roster in Formula 1: Atlassian as title partner, VAST for data infrastructure, Keeper for identity security and, since February, Claude as Official Thinking Partner. There is no database or backend-platform partner on the car. Supabase's own release credits Claude Code as the top creator of new databases this year, so the introduction runs through a relationship Williams already has.
brief_data.deal_arch_para: Entry as Official Developer Platform Partner. <font name='Poppins-Bold' size='9.5'>THREE YEARS</font>, 2027-2029, covering the next raise or a listing window. Estimated $3-5M a year, part-payable in platform credits. Scope: livery placement, developer activations at the British GP and the US rounds, content with the Claude programme, first refusal on a database category in 2030.
brief_data.why_now_callout: <font name='Poppins-Bold' size='9'>WHY NOW</font>  The round closed on 4 June; brand budgets reset in the quarter after a raise, and this is the largest in the company's history. The British GP on 5 July is Williams' home race and falls inside the window; teams settle their 2027 rosters in the fourth quarter.
brief_data.decision_maker_bio: Copplestone co-founded Supabase in 2020 with CTO Ant Wilson and fronts every raise; a first sports partnership is his call. Path: Rory Wilding, COO and Chief Commercial Officer, and Scott Buxton, CFO. No chief marketing officer is listed; marketing is developer-led.
brief_data.opening_angle_intro: Lead with the Claude Code number.
brief_data.opening_angle_quote: “Paul, Claude Code is the biggest creator of Supabase databases this year, and Claude already races on the Williams. The developer-platform lane there is open and the British GP is five weeks out. 25 minutes to see the numbers?”
